notes: Copyright Proxima Enterprises Inc.; describes the website build as Early Access and the Steam version as the 1.0 release with Workshop support; players craft character personalities and behaviors.

name: Moodles
notes: Moodle list and effects: hungry, thirsty, panic, bored, stressed, unhappy, heavy load, endurance, tired, hyperthermia, hypothermia, windchill, wet, injured, pain, bleeding, has a cold, sick; zombie infection always fatal in an unmodified game.

name: ALPHA RELEASE! WHOO!
notes: Public release of the free Proof of Concept Demo Alpha 0.4.0 (XNA); adjustable simulation speed, creature and DNA inspection, species statistics over time, Tree of Life view, move, feed, and remove tools, bundled Mod Maker.

name: Species 0.7.0 Released!
notes: Free alpha; skeleton analyzed for internal forces and torques to charge energy costs; creatures eat only within head reach; rovers feed or kill by genetic distance to a target genome and can be programmed to deforest or fertilize; climate control devices make cold, hot, fertile, or dead ground; fences.

name: Devblog #5: Thrive vs Species
notes: Describes Species (single developer Quasar, free alpha) genes stored as numbers; most mutations add a random value in [-1, 1] times a modifier for background mutation rate and radiation; species defined by interbreeding within genetic distance, splitting only when intermediates die out; stamina from joint torques.

name: AI Storytellers
notes: Storytellers weigh colony wealth, colonist and animal counts, recent deaths or wounds, and time since the last major event. Incident chance = base chance x population-intent factor (8.0 at 0 colonists falling to -1.0 at 20). Cassandra escalates in cycles, Phoebe leaves longer gaps, Randy follows no pattern and has a 0.20 minimum factor.

name: Backstories
notes: All pawns get a childhood backstory; pawns generated at 20 or older also get an adulthood one. Backstories add flat skill modifiers, enable or disable work types, and grant or forbid traits. 25% of regular pawns and all faction leaders first try a fixed player-made bio, else shuffled backstories.

name: Goodwill
notes: Faction goodwill -100 to 100; hostile at -75 or below, ally at 75 or above until it drops to 0; civil outlanders drift into -50..50 (0.4 per day down, 0.2 up); returning a prisoner +12; trade +1 per 500 silver; gifts +1 per 40-160 silver; arresting a visitor sets -75; pirates fixed at -100; calling a caravan costs 15.

name: Health
notes: Capacities from body parts: consciousness below 30% keeps a pawn from waking; moving below 15% incapacitates; each arm gives half of manipulation; blood pumping or digestion at 0% is fatal; poor tending raises scarring and infection risk; bionic leg +12.5% moving; base healing 8 damage per day.

name: Inspiration
notes: Inspirations need mood above 49%; mean days between them = 410 - 400 x mood fraction (210 at 50%, 10 at 100%); one at a time; weighted by passion 1, 2.5, 5; inspired creativity raises one item two quality levels; inspired trade +18% prices; work frenzy x1.8 work speed; most last 8 days.

name: Mental break
notes: Base thresholds minor 35%, major 20% (4/7 of minor), extreme 5% (1/7 of minor); traits shift the minor threshold, capped 1-50%; mean time between breaks below each threshold about 4 days (minor), 0.8 (major), 0.5 (extreme).

name: Mood
notes: Mood 0-100% is base mood plus net thoughts; base mood by difficulty from 22 to 42; the bar moves toward its target at up to +12 per hour rising and -8 per hour falling and pauses while asleep; break risk bands below 35%, 20%, 5%.

name: Raid points
notes: Raid points = (wealth points + pawn points) x threat scale x starting factor x adaptation factor, capped at 10,000, minimum 35. Storyteller wealth counts items, creatures, and 50% of buildings; wealth points 0 at 14,000 up to 4,200 at 1,000,000; 15-200 points per colonist; threat scale 0.1-2.2 by preset; starting factor 0.7 through day 10; adaptation factor about 0.4-1.47, lowered by deaths and downings.

name: Room
notes: Rooms enclosed by walls, doors, vents, coolers, or natural rock; max 36 map regions or 5,184 tiles; roles scored from contents (dining 12 per table, workshop 27 per workbench, bedroom invalid with more than one unassigned bed); beauty = total beauty / weighted size (size if >40, else 20 + size/2); impressiveness combines wealth, beauty, space, and cleanliness with log scaling and min-weighting.

name: Skills
notes: Levels 0-20; XP to next level 1,000 at level 0 rising to 30,000 at 19; passion learning 35%, 100%, 150% and +8 or +14 mood during related work; decay above level 9 from 30 to 3,600 XP per day; daily cap 4,000 XP per skill, then gains x20%; construction speed 50% plus 15% per level; incapable work types.

name: Social
notes: Opinion -100 to 100; rival below -20, friend above 20; chitchat about +0.66 stacking to +10; deep talk +15, insult -15, slight -5 for 20 days; insult odds up to 6x at -100 opinion; social fight 4% per insult; parent +30, sibling +20; lover +35, spouse +30, ex -15, breakup -50; romance attempts every 12 days for pawns over 16, beauty x0.3 to x2.3; rebuff -10 and -15.

name: Stockpile
notes: Stockpile priorities low, normal, preferred, important, critical; haulers bring items to higher-priority stockpiles with space, including items already stored in lower ones.

name: Thoughts
notes: Memory thoughts list mood effect, expiry in days, stack limit, and stack multiplier (mostly 0.75). Examples: Colonist lost 6 days, 5 stacks; My son died -20 for 30 days; My friend died -10 for 20 days, scaled by relation; expectations +18 (low) to -12 (royal); lavish meal +12, raw food -7; some traits nullify thoughts.

name: Time
notes: 60 ticks per second at normal speed; speeds x3, x6, and x15 (ultrafast only in development mode); runs as close to target as hardware allows; 2,500 ticks per hour, 60,000 per day; 15-day quadrums, 4 per 60-day year; Space pauses.

name: Work
notes: Work tab in standard mode (checkmarks, columns further left more important) or manual priorities 1-4; all available work at one priority is done before the next; ties resolve left to right; blank cells never done; incapable types excluded; allowed areas restrict where work is taken.

name: Cube: A Roblox View of 3D Intelligence
notes: 3D shape tokenizer as foundation for Roblox developers; text-to-shape, shape-to-text, text-to-scene; LLM integration for scene reasoning.

name: Roblox Cube repository
notes: Cube 3D v0.1 2025-03, v0.5 2025-07 (bounding-box conditioning, ~2.8M additional synthetic assets), CubePart 2026-05 (part-controllable, usable with animation, physics, scripts); OBJ output; 16-24 GB VRAM.

name: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
authors: Bernardino Romera-Paredes;Mohammadamin Barekatain;Alexander Novikov;et al.;Alhussein Fawzi
notes: FunSearch: frozen LLM proposes programs, evaluator scores them, island-based program database; cap set of size 512 in dimension 8; online bin-packing heuristics beat first fit and best fit.

name: Predicting Game Difficulty and Churn Without Players
authors: Shaghayegh Roohi;Asko Relas;Jari Takatalo;Henri Heiskanen;Perttu Hämäläinen
notes: Deep RL agents estimate level difficulty in Angry Birds Dream Blast; a population model with skill, persistence, and boredom predicts per-level pass and churn rates.

name: How a single game trailer turned the tide for Factorio
notes: After the February 2013 Indiegogo campaign the team had a purchasable alpha version on sale; alpha sales barely covered living expenses for almost a year.

name: Learning to Simulate Complex Physics with Graph Networks
authors: Alvaro Sanchez-Gonzalez;Jonathan Godwin;Tobias Pfaff;Rex Ying;Jure Leskovec;Peter W. Battaglia
notes: GNS: particles as graph nodes with learned message passing for fluids, rigid solids, deformables; trained on one-step targets, generalizes to thousands of steps and 10x more particles; training noise limits drift.

name: Alternate recipes
notes: 106 alternate recipes; each crash-site Hard Drive scanned in the MAM offers a choice of two; drives can be stored in a library and re-rolled once; a few alternates come from MAM research instead.

name: Blueprint Designer
notes: Introduced in patch 0.7.0.0; Mk.1 (40 x 40 m) unlocks at Tier 4, Mk.2 and Mk.3 added in 1.0; saved blueprints appear in a build-menu tab and draw materials from the designer's storage then the player's inventory.

name: Clock speed
notes: Clock speed settable from 1% to 250%; each Power Shard raises the cap by 50% up to three shards; power scales nonlinearly with exponent 1.321928 (changed from 1.6 in 0.7.0.0), so 250% draws 335.77% of base power.

name: Conveyor Belts
notes: Belt throughput Mk.1 to Mk.6: 60, 120, 270, 480, 780, and 1,200 items per minute.

name: Drone
notes: Drones provide long-range low-throughput transport between a home Drone Port and one linked port; 9 inventory slots; fuelled by batteries or packaged fuels, with faster speeds for higher-value fuel; one drone unloads at a time.

name: Pipeline
notes: Pipeline Mk.1 carries 300 m3/min and Mk.2 600 m3/min; liquids need head lift (about 1.3 m to fill a level pipe); pumps add head lift; gases need none.

name: Power
notes: A grid trips when consumption exceeds production and Power Storage is empty, stopping every connected building until the fuse is reset; buildings do not slow during shortages; Power Storage holds 100 MWh; generators from 30 MW (Biomass Burner) to 2,500 MW (Nuclear Power Plant); idle buildings draw 0.1 MW.

name: Resource node
notes: All resource nodes are infinite; purity multipliers impure 0.5x, normal 1.0x, pure 2.0x.

name: Space Elevator
notes: Five Project Assembly phases unlock tiers 3-4, 5-6, 7-8, 9, and the ending; phase 1 needs 50 Smart Plating, phase 5 needs Nuclear Pasta, Biochemical Sculptors, AI Expansion Servers, and Ballistic Warp Drives; progress is shared in multiplayer; completing phase 5 launches Project Assembly.

name: Student of Games: A unified learning algorithm for both perfect and imperfect information games
authors: Martin Schmid;Matej Moravčík;Neil Burch;Rudolf Kadlec;Josh Davidson;Kevin Waugh;Nolan Bard;Finbarr Timbers;Marc Lanctot;G. Zacharias Holland;Elnaz Davoodi;Alden Christianson;Michael Bowling
notes: Guided search, self-play learning, and game-theoretic reasoning in one sound algorithm; strong in chess and Go, beat the strongest open heads-up no-limit agent, and beat the prior best Scotland Yard agent.

name: Mastering Atari, Go, chess and shogi by planning with a learned model
authors: Julian Schrittwieser;Ioannis Antonoglou;Thomas Hubert;Karen Simonyan;Laurent Sifre;Simon Schmitt;Arthur Guez;Edward Lockhart;Demis Hassabis;Thore Graepel;Timothy Lillicrap;David Silver
notes: MuZero: learned representation, dynamics, and prediction networks planned over with MCTS, without being given the rules; preprint November 2019.

name: OUT NOW: Autonauts (Denki)
notes: Created by Gary Penn and Aaron Puzey at Denki; robots controlled with a Scratch-inspired visual language; Colonise, Free, and Creative modes; full release added a campaign, transport, animal husbandry, multipart bots, and expanded research.

name: Screeps blog: Indiegogo updates, November 2014 to February 2015
notes: Paginated blog listing (position may shift). In late 2014 the browser Simulation mode was the playable version, called 'only a demo' on 2014-11-25; the Indiegogo campaign ended 2014-12-31; a ranked Survival mode open to all was announced live on 2015-01-21.

name: Game situation review: December 11, 2015
notes: States 'A year has passed since the initial launch of the game' and introduces the Public Test Realm; a January 2016 post on the same page notes a Steam version giving lifetime MMO access with a 10 CPU limit.

name: Screeps private server released!
notes: Announces the open-source private server and that the game would exit Steam Early Access with a full release on 16 November 2016.

name: Control
notes: Room Controller Levels 1-8 unlock spawns, extensions, towers, storage, links, labs, terminal, factory, observer, and nuker at cumulative upgrade energy; unupgraded controllers downgrade; Global Control Level sets claimable rooms and CPU (10 per level up to 300) and is never lost.

name: How does CPU limit work
notes: Per-tick CPU limit (20 without CPU Unlock, otherwise tied to Global Control Level); unused CPU accumulates in a bucket of up to 10,000; a tick may use up to 500 CPU from the bucket; scripts are terminated at the limit.

name: Creeps
notes: Bodies of up to 50 parts (WORK, MOVE, CARRY, ATTACK, RANGED_ATTACK, HEAL, CLAIM, TOUGH); lifespan 1,500 ticks; spawn budget 300 energy plus extensions; non-MOVE parts add fatigue 1/2/10 on road/plain/swamp and each MOVE part removes 2 per tick; 100 hits per part.

name: Understanding game loop, time and ticks
notes: Each player's main module runs once per tick against a fixed game state; commands queue and are applied together at the end of the tick with conflicts resolved by priority; globals are erased between ticks.

name: Introduction
notes: One persistent world of 50x50-cell rooms grouped into shards; plain movement cost 2, swamp 10, road 1; energy sources regenerate every 300 ticks; at most 3 spawns per room; a first spawn grants safe mode.

name: Market
notes: Terminals trade through public buy and sell orders in credits with a 5% order fee; the party executing a deal pays an energy transfer cost that grows with distance; NPC terminals sit at highway crossroads.

name: Crossing the uncanny valley of conversational voice
notes: Conversational Speech Model: Llama-variant backbone (1B, 3B, 8B) plus small decoder over Mimi split-RVQ tokens at 12.5 Hz; about one million hours of mostly English audio. CMOS: no preference vs human without context; human recordings preferred with 90 s of context. No turn-taking modeling; Apache 2.0 release announced.

name: An Extensible, Data-Oriented Architecture for High-Performance, Many-World Simulation
authors: Brennan Shacklett;Luc Guy Rosenzweig;Bidipta Sarkar;Zhiqiang Xie;Andrew Szot;Erik Wijmans;Vladlen Koltun;Dhruv Batra;Kayvon Fatahalian
notes: Madrona batch ECS engine. Project page: Hide and Seek over 1.9M steps/s, Overcooked-AI 40M steps/s, Hanabi 20M steps/s (RTX 4090); 2-3 orders of magnitude over open-source CPU baselines, 5-33x over 32-thread CPU baselines.

name: Modding
notes: The game loads mods natively with the ShapezShifter API; mods are published to and auto-downloaded from Steam Workshop.

name: Operator Level
notes: Endless goal lines after milestones and jobs; cost grows exponentially per level (Fluids & Painting starts at 15,000 shapes with 18% growth); levels reward Platform Units, Blueprint Points, and Research Points unless copy/paste is free or the platform limit is off.

name: Shapes
notes: Layers hold 4 parts (6 in the Hexagonal scenario); shapes have 1 to 4 layers (5 in Insane); part types include circle, square, star, diamond, pin, and crystal; nine colors; shape codes list layers bottom to top; floating parts are not allowed; separating crystals shatters them.
